newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Although any increase in foreign ownership limits for Australia's media has been consistently rejected by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and Communications Minister Richard Alston, ministers at last week's Federal Cabinet meeting gave serious consideraton to the issue for the first time. Page 1.

In what is a major blow to the Federal Opposition, Labor frontbencher Carmen Lawrence has been charged with perjury in relation to the 1995 Royal Commission into the Penny Easton affair. Lawrence faces three charges relating to providing false or misleadng information, and last night announced she would step down in accordance with an agreement held with Opposition Leader Kim Beazley. Page 3.

Following a three-hour meeting with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission chairman Gatjill Djerrkura, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday agreed to consider some proposals put forward by Aboriginal negotiators, but refused to budge on the cental issues of his 10-point Wik plan. Page 3.

Following a decision by two judges of the Industrial Relations Court, compulsory employer superannuation contributions will be counted as part of salary for the purposes of a cap on access to federal unfair dismissal remedies, meaning thousands of employees could be excluded. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Opposition Environment Spokeswoman and former West Australian Premier Carmen Lawrence was last night summonsed to appear in the Perth Magistrates Court on Thursday after she was charged with three counts of perjury following her evidence to the 1995 Easton Royal Commission. Former Labor Leader in the West Australian Upper House John Halden and former Lawrence staffer Ed Russell were also charged, with one count of perjury each. Page 1.

Following the release yesterday of an independent review of the Commonwealth's Palliative Care Program, which warned that the uncertainty of funding for such services threatened the quality of care for terminally ill patients, Federal Health Minister Michel Wooldridge suggested palliative care services will be expanded to help those at home. Page 1.

Herb Elliott, one of Australia's greatest Olympic athletics legends who will shortly give up his job as president of Puma North America to assume a position with the Australian Olympic Committee, was in Australia yesterday, and said there were some encouraging signs this country would regain the mantle of sporting greatness it held 40 years ago. Page 1.

The Revenue Committee of Cabinet is to determine the fate of the former Keating Government's "LAW" tax cuts this week, a move which may see the Howard Government introducing a special tax rebate on savings for low and middle income earners as it wraps up the details for the upcoming Federal Budget. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Former West Australian premier Carmen Lawrence and State Labor MLC John Halden were last night charged with perjury concerning evidence submitted to the Marks Royal Commission into the Penny Easton affair, and have been summonsed to appear in the Perth Court of Petty Sessions on Thursday. Page 1.

According to a controversial new book entitled Pauline Hanson, The Truth, published by Independent MP Pauline Hanson's supporters to raise money for her new political party, Pauline Hanson - One Nation, Aborigines who lived in the Palmer River area in norhern Queensland last century cannibalised family members. The book has come under heavy criticism, with calls the cannibalism claims have been made without evidence. Page 1.

Under the recommendations of a review obtained by the Herald which comes as part of the Federal Government's immigration shake-up, Australian firms will have greater freedom to recruit skilled workers overseas using fixed contracts, rather than employing them permanently. Page 1.

New South Wales yesterday rejected a Federal scheme to pay secondary schools to act as job finders, labelling the proposal "vague and unclear". The criticism comes as Federal Schools Minister David Kemp calls for greater freedom for public schools in choosing staff and reporting on student performance. Page 2.
THE AGE

Former West Australian Premier Carmen Lawrence has stepped down from the Federal Opposition frontbench after being charged last night with three counts of perjury arising from the Marks Royal Commission into the events surrounding the suicide of Perth lawer Penny Easton, but has denied the charges and will remain in Parliament. Page 1.

In a deal which will allow the Victorian Government to repay more than A$3 billion of debt and will add between A$200 million and A$400 million to the State Budget's bottom-line, the Loy Yang A power station has been sold to a group headed by United State-based CMS Energy for a price believed to be around A$4.75 billion. Page 1.

George Marcus, the 44-year-old Egyptian national whose body was found on a pavement in Box Hill North on Sunday, was known by family and friends as a respectable businessman within the legal fraternity, but according to the Law Institute of Victoria, which began receiving complaints about Marcus from 1994, the father of three never held a certificate to practice law. Page 1.

Federal Schools, Vocational Education and Training Minister David Kemp announced a A$200 million Government program yesterday aimed at allowing schools to compete with private agencies to help find students employment. Under the plan, schools would receive an upfront payment to help a student find a job, then another when a suitable position was found. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
